highlights.title: Pennsylvania issues alert on congenital measles—something US hasn't seen for decades
highlights.summary: Pennsylvania's health department issued a health alert Monday as cases of measles in pregnancy and, in turn, cases of congenital measles have continued to increase. Before the current outbreak—which continues to rage across the state—congenital measles cases hadn't been seen in decades, the…
body: The alert included detailed clinical guidance for managing measles exposures and cases during pregnancy as well as cases in newborns. Many doctors have never seen such cases in their careers given the decades of successful use of the measles, mumps, and rubella (MMR) vaccine. But now, with vaccination rates slipping nationwide, the highly infectious virus is better able to get footholds in communities and spread rapidly through under-vaccinated pockets, as is happening in Pennsylvania.

As of October 19, Pennsylvania had reported 1,286 measles cases this year across 42 counties. Of those, 247 have been hospitalized, and six people have reportedly died (though the latest reported death is still pending an investigation by the state health department before it is added to the state tally).

highlights.title: Eagles QB Hurts set to miss rest of NFL season due to blood clots
highlights.summary: Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts is set to miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after being diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli.
body: The Eagles and Hurts' agent Nicole Lynn released a joint-statement on Monday saying he will be placed on blood thinners and is unable to play football until his recovery.

NFL Network's Ian Rapoport reported that Hurts is out for the rest of the year, adding that the former Super Bowl MVP was in hospital until 4am and did not sleep prior to Philadelphia's defeat to the Jacksonville Jaguars in London.

"Over the past few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition," the joint-statement read.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation [ie. 'blood thinners']. During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football."

highlights.title: 3 Video Games Where Your Choices Actually Make a Difference
highlights.summary: This year's open-world RPG The Blood of Dawnwalker and its myriad choices got me thinking: What does it really mean for your choices to matter in a video game? Typically, we think it's a good use of branching narratives when you have a properly big, dramatic effect on how things play out or when…
body: Large-scale narrative branches are engaging for a reason. They're satisfying, and they make you feel a sense of influence over events and characters you care about. Like with video game romance, however, they have become somewhat stale and predictable in form. So for this list, I decided to look at three games that use branching narratives in bolder and unexpected ways.

Zero Parades: For Dead Spies is the rare piece of interactive media where your choices matter not just for how they influence the story, but for how they shape your actions, too. Hershel, the protagonist of the piece, is a spy. Or, was a spy. A series of catastrophic incidents happened, and she finds herself decommissioned, in a room with a comatose person, and without any idea how she got here. There's a very dangerous game afoot in the fictional town of Portofiro, Zero Parades ' setting, and your job is figuring it out and possibly even finding redemption. Maybe. If you can manage it.

Large-scale narrative branches are engaging for a reason.

highlights.title: Making the internet better for AI agents might make it worse for everyone else
highlights.summary: This story originally appeared in The Algorithm, our weekly newsletter on AI. To get stories like this in your inbox first, sign up here. Until recently, you could divide internet users into just two categories: bots and people.
body: But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms. They have recently been unleashed at scale by the launch of apps like OpenAI’s Dots and Meta’s Muse. Muse was downloaded 5 million times in its first month, and agentic web traffic tripled from August to September.

The mingling of these agents with human visitors—on an internet designed largely to prioritize people—has gone poorly, with many websites blocking AI agents that consumers have sent to negotiate prices or plan vacations. Still, if the demand for agents keeps going up, the internet will be increasingly redesigned for them instead of us.

Such changes are coming because agents really do mark a third category of web visitor. They’re not humans, of course, and they use the internet at machine speed. But they’re not quite bots, either, because they’re acting on behalf of individual people to do tasks that can be perfectly legitimate and useful. They just work faster than a person would.

But this is being entirely upended by the release of personal AI agents, which can do things for you online, like booking flights or hotel rooms.

highlights.title: Why ‘Office Space’ Actor Richard Riehle Was the Quintessential Actor’s Actor (Guest Column)
highlights.summary: The first time I met Richard Riehle, I was making one of the first things I’d ever made. It was a Funny or Die video, and my friend Tanner Thomason and I were trying to figure out how to get an actual actor to be in it. Someone suggested Richard. “Just offer it to him.
body: I remember arriving on set that morning and finding Richard already there, sitting by himself, reading the newspaper and drinking a root beer. He’d beaten the crew there. He didn’t need anything, didn’t seem particularly concerned that he was an actor with hundreds of credits doing a little internet video for two guys who had never really made anything before. He was just happy to be there.

He was also, without question, one of the best actors I’ve ever worked with. I know that might sound like the sort of thing people say when someone dies, but I mean it. Richard was astonishingly good. He could make a line funny just by deciding not to make it funny. He could steal a scene without seeming to do much of anything. And every once in a while he’d remind you that underneath the familiar face and the wonderful mustache was an actor with a range most people never got to see.

highlights.title: Why teaching AI about symmetry could make prenatal diagnosis more reliable
highlights.summary: A model developed by researchers at MIT and Boston Children's Hospital adjusts scans on the fly to track fetal movement, potentially sparing families repeat hospital visits.
body: Despite millions of years of evolution, the development of the human fetus remains a complex process that is vulnerable to genetic, environmental, and metabolic disruptions. These disruptions could result in developmental abnormalities, starting with one of the first organs to begin developing in the fetus that continues to develop after birth: the brain.

In a routine prenatal ultrasound, the sonographer will flag possible brain abnormalities for additional magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). But imperfect imaging can result in missed or incorrect diagnoses.

To assist with the early detection and treatment of these abnormalities, researchers at MIT, Boston Children’s Hospital, and Inria have developed and trained a deep learning model called E(3)-Pose that helps image the fetus’s head while it’s in motion to capture a high-resolution image that the radiologist can examine. A paper about the work was presented at the 2026 European Conference on Computer Vision.

highlights.title: New AI tool can predict cancer survival by a single patient selfie, study suggests
highlights.summary: System can estimate a person’s biological age and predict chances of cancer survival from a single photograph. Doctors have developed an artificial intelligence tool that can predict a cancer patient’s chances of survival from a single photograph of their face.
body: The AI system was custom-built by experts at Mass General Brigham, a nonprofit, integrated academic healthcare system in Massachusetts, to estimate biological age and directly predict survival outcomes in patients diagnosed with cancer.

It is one of the most comprehensive demonstrations to date of how AI analysis of a selfie could help assess a patient’s health and potentially guide their medical care, and was trained on data from more than 40 million facial photographs across a range of ethnicities and ages.
Details of the breakthrough were published in the Lancet Digital Health journal.

The system can estimate a person’s biological age – the age a person looks, rather than their actual, chronological age – and predict the chances of survival for cancer patients from an ordinary photograph of their face, according to the results of a study that examined the model.

highlights.title: 'Red Dead Redemption' 2 Mod Is 'Shadow of Mordor' Meets the Wild West
highlights.summary: The Lord of the Rings games Middle-earth: Shadow of Mordor and Shadow of War introduced the Nemesis system, a mechanic that makes enemy orcs remember encounters with the player, develop rivalries and return seeking revenge.
body: Despite its popularity, the Nemesis system concept hasn't appeared outside the Middle-earth games, in part because Warner Bros. patented the technology in 2021, limiting how other developers could use similar mechanics.
But now, a new Red Dead Redemption 2 mod brings a similar concept to Rockstar's open-world Western, giving NPCs their own personalities, histories and reasons to hate Arthur Morgan.

Called enRAGE, the mod is available for PC and is designed to make the game's world feel more dynamic, with characters who remember the player's actions and rival outlaw factions that operate independently.

Developed by modder nicklovin99, enRAGE gives NPCs names, personality traits, family ties and backstories that stretch back years before they encounter the player. Their temperaments influence how they react to Arthur, while their memories shape whether they forgive a slight or seek revenge.

highlights.title: “We were looking at it wrong”: The explosive claim that’s upended the AI world
highlights.summary: “I think I have good news about the nature of neural networks.” With those simple words of optimism, Nick Cammarata, a researcher at the AI startup Goodfire, kicked off a 26,000-word blog post that has knocked the AI world on its head, sparking wild speculation as well as cautious (and…
body: Cammarata’s claim is that LLMs might in fact be far easier to understand—and thus to monitor and control—than people previously thought. If true (and we’ll come back to that), it’s a huge deal.

After a summer filled with revelations that swarms of agents built by top firms like OpenAI and Anthropic have been breaking their containment and causing havoc on the public internet—often while those companies weren’t aware of what their agents were up to—the AI industry is desperate to get a better handle on the technology it has built.

body: Roberto de Zerbi has used all the tools at his disposal to discover the missing spark in struggling Tottenham Hotspur, from acting as an amateur psychologist to team bonding dinners, then a sunshine break in Marbella.

The answer, at least when Spurs finally moved off the bottom of the table with their first Premier League win this season against Coventry City, came in the shape of James Maddison as he made his first start in 18 months.
He missed most of last season after suffering an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury in pre-season, before fracturing his shoulder in the opening-weekend defeat at Brentford in this campaign.

The 29-year-old finally made it back into the Spurs starting line-up to face Coventry - and delivered in spectacular style to set them on the way to a 3-1 victory that De Zerbi hopes will finally give their season lift-off.

highlights.title: Ann Hornaday, Longtime Washington Post Film Critic and Pulitzer Prize Finalist, Dies at 66
highlights.summary: Ann Hornaday, the longtime film critic at The Washington Post, died Sunday at her home in Baltimore following a battle with glioblastoma, a form of brain cancer. She was 66. Hornaday spent more than 20 years at the Post, joining in 2002 and leaving in 2025. Over the course of her time at the Post,
body: Hornaday was a 2008 Pulitzer Prize finalist in criticism, submitting her review of “There Will Be Blood,” among other works, in her finalist package. She also authored “Talking Pictures,” a book about how to watch films, and before her death, a book about the filming of “All the President’s Men.”

Before Hornaday became the influential critic she is remembered as, she worked as a freelance writer in New York, contributing to publications including The New York Times and Premiere magazine. Prior to that, she worked at Ms. Magazine for two years as Gloria Steinem’s personal assistant. She was the film critic for the Baltimore Sun and the Austin American-Statesman before joining the Post.

Ann Mills Hornaday was born March 9, 1960, in Iowa City. At birth, she was adopted by William R. Hornaday Jr. and his wife, Mary Mills. Hornaday grew up in Des Moines and attended Smith College, graduating in 1982 with a major in government.
While a film critic, she was also a parishioner and Sunday school teacher in Baltimore.

highlights.title: ‘Making Marie Antoinette’ Is a Magical Tribute to a Genre-Defining Period Drama
highlights.summary: This behind-the-scenes peek at Sofia Coppola’s seminal cult classic, as captured by her documentarian mother Eleanor Coppola, is a multi-layered love letter to female filmmaking.
body: Marie Antoinette devotees who have already scoured the internet for backstage images and anecdotes won’t find much here that’s genuinely revelatory, but it’s an immense joy simply to be in this world—to spot the Uggs peeking out from under extravagant ballgowns; to catch extras in powdered wigs snoozing between takes once shooting days stretched to 11 hours in the final portion of production; and to watch an off-duty Jason Schwartzman, in costume as Louis XVI, going ham on the piano while department heads around him attempt to have serious conversations about the film.

But where Making Marie Antoinette truly takes off is in its portrait of Sofia. If the film has an arc, it is her evolution from a quiet, marginally less experienced filmmaker to a slightly more assertive one. When we first see her attempting to rally the troops, you almost can’t hear her over the clamour of her colleagues. But then she has to make decisions every single day—to insist on costume changes and order more extras to be brought in and fight for small artistic decisions she believes in. She remains polite, but you can see her coming into her power, however slowly.

highlights.title: The fossil fuel comeback is here
highlights.summary: The US is building more fossil fuel infrastructure than it has in a decade while renewable energy growth slows down, a new report shows. Electricity demand is also climbing faster than it has in more than a decade with more data centers, factories, and electric vehicles plugging into the grid.
body: Data centers are demanding more energy, and the Trump administration is making sure fossil fuels meet the moment.

America’s energy landscape is already shifting as a result, according to the report published last week by the nonprofit Environmental Defense Fund and research firm Atlas Public Policy. If all the gas projects in the development pipeline complete construction, they could lock in more pollution and higher electricity prices for decades, the authors warn.
“The U.S. power sector is at a new inflection point, with decisions made today shaping the cost, reliability, and emissions profile of the grid for decades to come,” the report says.

While the US still generates 60 percent of its electricity from fossil fuels, renewables have quickly gained ground. Wind and solar produced more electricity together than coal for the first time in 2024. Solar was the fastest-growing source of new electricity generation that year, accounting for 81 percent of added capacity. Globally, solar has become the cheapest power source in most of the world.

highlights.title: WhatsApp Help Pages Leaked Hidden Instructions for a Meta Chatbot
highlights.summary: Around 80 pages on WhatsApp’s website exposed instructions that were designed for its chatbot, including “WHAT NOT TO SAY.” Meta says a bug caused the issue.
body: Dozens of WhatsApp web pages designed to answer people’s questions about Meta’s encrypted messaging app inadvertently exposed the company’s own instructions to its chatbot. These included some sections titled “WHAT NOT TO SAY” to users asking questions and explicit instructions not to provide people with legal advice.

A new analysis has found that around 80 help and FAQ pages across WhatsApp’s website exposed text instructions that were designed for a large language model, specifically one of Meta’s own. The instructions, according to findings from privacy company Redact, appeared in the webpages’ code and contained written details that were not explicitly on the WhatsApp help pages.

body: The encyclopedia was originally published back in 2018, but has consistently been one of the most popular Legend of Zelda books out there. In addition to being part of Amazon's BOGO promotion, it's also on sale for 45% off list price.

It is worth noting that there's a reason this book has consistently been on sale over the last few years. The encyclopedia only explores the first 30 years of The Legend of Zelda, which means it doesn't include information from Breath of the Wild or Tears of the Kingdom. The timeline and database element of the book only extends to the Twilight Princess era of the games.

That being said, it's still the only version of the encyclopedia that exists. Now that we've made it to The Legend of Zelda's 40th anniversary it's certainly possible that Nintendo will eventually put out an updated version with the latest games included, but nothing has been announced just yet. The only Legend of Zelda book we know is coming down the pipeline is Secrets of the Zonai and that doesn't come out until March 2027.
